routingDryRun.bannerDetail: A test never creates work, reserves stock or contacts a carrier. It uses the same engine as real routing.
routingDryRun.compareNoChange: The draft places every line exactly where the saved rules do.
routingDryRun.explanationEmpty: No rules ran, so nothing was filtered or ranked.
routingDryRun.orderSearchError: Orders could not be searched just now.
routingDryRun.resultInputNote: Country, postcode, lines and delivery method only. No buyer details reach the rules.
routingDryRun.resultLinesHeading: Where each line would ship from
routingDryRun.resultRoutableSplit: The order is split across locations. That is expected, not an error.
routingDryRun.resultUnfulfillableNote: Unsourced units can only be resolved as a refund or a return, never as a partial cancellation.

skipReasons.mirrored-before-routing: It was already created in your product master before routing was on.
skipReasons.own-shop-order: It came from your own shop, which already handles it.
skipReasons.shipped-by-other-system: Another system has been told to ship it.

routingDryRun.skippedNote: The result below only shows where the rules would send it if they ran.
routingDryRun.skippedTitle: Live routing would not route this order
routingDryRun.skippedUnknown: OpenLinker records a reason for this that this screen does not describe.

afterActionHints.line-split: Different items can ship from different locations. Each item still ships whole, from one place.
afterActionHints.no-split: The whole order ships from a single location - or not at all.
afterActionHints.quantity-split: Even a single item's quantity can be split - e.g. 2 units from one location, 3 from another.

kindHints.filter: Filter - rules out locations that cannot do the job.
kindHints.sort: Sort - ranks whichever locations are left.

nameHints.country-served: Only keeps a location if it's registered in the same country the order ships to - that is about where the location physically is, not which countries it is set up to ship to.
nameHints.in-stock: Rules out any location with no stock of at least one item in this order.
nameHints.least-splits: Prefers a single location that can fulfil the whole order, to avoid splitting it.
nameHints.most-complete: Prefers the location that can fulfil the most items in this order.
nameHints.nearest: Ranks by how close the postcode is to the delivery address - not the real driving or shipping distance. With PII storage off there is no postcode to compare, so it falls back to ranking by country alone.
nameHints.not-blocked-by-reject: Rules out a location that already turned this order down.
nameHints.priority: Ranks locations in the order you choose.

sourcingRuleConflict.forbidden: You do not have permission to change sourcing rules.
sourcingRuleConflict.notFound: This sourcing rule no longer exists.

sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.deleteFailed: The rule could not be deleted.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.deletesForGood: This deletes the rule for good, including its history.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.description: Every rule below it moves up one step.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.removalLoosens: Removing this rule lifts your only limit on splitting: orders could start splitting more than they do today (up to {ceiling}). No other active rule currently prevents that. Retiring has the same effect as deleting here, because a retired rule is not evaluated either.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.retireFailed: The rule could not be retired.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.retireInsteadHint: If you just want to stop using it, retire it instead - it stays on the list, keeps its history, and can coexist with a replacement.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.retireRetired: This rule is already retired, so it is not being evaluated. Deleting removes it and its history for good.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.retireScheduled: This rule has not started yet, so there is nothing to retire: it is not deciding any orders, and an end date before its start date is refused. Delete it, or change its start date in Edit.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.retireUnrecognised: This rule cannot be retired because this version of OpenLinker no longer recognises it - it is already being ignored. Deleting is the only way to remove it.
sourcingRuleDeleteDialog.title: Delete “{label}”?

sourcingRuleDialog.addSubtitle: This will be rule {position} - everything above it is checked first.
sourcingRuleDialog.countryServedWarning: If you run one warehouse that ships to several countries, this rule rules it out for every order NOT placed in that warehouse’s own country - including orders you would normally be happy to ship. It is built for “one warehouse per country”, not “one warehouse serving many”.
sourcingRuleDialog.editSubtitle: Rule {position} - everything above it is checked first.
sourcingRuleDialog.endsOnDescription: Setting this to a past date retires the rule while keeping it for history.
sourcingRuleDialog.loosenDescription: No other active rule currently limits splitting to {before}. Once you save, orders may be split more than they are today (up to {after}).
sourcingRuleDialog.loosens: Based on what you have set here, this would allow MORE splitting overall: {after} instead of today's {before} - no other active rule limits it that tightly.
sourcingRuleDialog.noSetup: This rule needs no extra setup.

picker.addLabel: Add a location to the priority list
picker.staleEntry: No location exists for this entry - it ranks nothing

sourcingRuleDialog.priorityDescription: Any location you do not add here is used last, after everything on this list.
sourcingRuleDialog.saveFailed: The rule could not be saved.
sourcingRuleDialog.stricter: Based on what you have set here, this makes splitting stricter overall: {after} (currently {before}).
sourcingRuleDialog.typeLocked: Cannot be changed. A rule’s type is part of what identifies it, so switching between Filter and Sort is not an edit - it is a different rule. Delete this one and add a new rule instead.
sourcingRuleDialog.unchanged: Based on what you have set here, splitting stays the same overall: {after}.

validation.afterActionRequired: Choose how far an order may be split
validation.endBeforeStart: The end date must be after the start date - otherwise this rule would never run
validation.filterAsSort: That rule filters locations; it cannot be used as a sort
validation.kindRequired: Choose whether this rule filters or sorts
validation.priorityEmpty: Add at least one location - a priority list with nothing in it ranks nothing
validation.priorityNotUsed: This rule does not use a location order, so the list must be empty
validation.sortAsFilter: That rule sorts locations; it cannot be used as a filter

sourcingRuleLockedDialog.description: This version of OpenLinker does not recognise this rule.
sourcingRuleLockedDialog.notUsed: It is saved, but it is not being used - orders route as if it were not here. Editing it would make it look active again, which would not be true.
sourcingRuleLockedDialog.remedy: Delete it and add a new rule instead. Its type and name are stored exactly as they were written, so they are worth quoting if you report this.
sourcingRuleLockedDialog.title: Cannot edit “{label}”

hints.active: This rule is deciding orders right now.
hints.retired: Kept for history. It decides nothing.
hints.scheduled: Saved, but it does not start deciding orders until its start date.
hints.unrecognised: This version of OpenLinker cannot evaluate this rule, so the router ignores it. It can be deleted, but not edited.

sourcingRulesPage.createLocationAdminOnly: Creating an inventory location requires an administrator account.
sourcingRulesPage.createLocationHint: Creates a single warehouse location, MAIN. Running it again creates nothing. It starts empty, so stock still has to be assigned to it before an order can actually be sent there, and its country is left blank on purpose - the rules read it, and a guessed country is worse than a missing one.
sourcingRulesPage.description: Rules run in order. Filters rule locations out; sorts rank whatever is left.
sourcingRulesPage.errorMessage: Your connections or locations could not be read just now. Nothing has changed - this is a loading problem, not a configuration one.
sourcingRulesPage.locationsTruncated: Showing {shown} of {total} locations. A priority rule can only rank the ones listed here, so a location past that point cannot be picked yet.
sourcingRulesPage.noLocationsMessage: Sourcing rules choose between your locations, and there are none active. Create one before authoring rules - until then every rule would rank an empty set.
sourcingRulesPage.noLocationsTitle: No locations to route to yet
sourcingRulesPage.noOmsMessage: Sourcing rules belong to the OpenLinker OMS connection, and there is not one yet. Enable the OMS first; its rules are managed from here afterwards.
sourcingRulesPage.noOmsTitle: The OpenLinker OMS is not enabled
sourcingRulesPage.wrongConnectionMessage: Sourcing rules only apply to your OpenLinker OMS connection - anything set up here would never be used. Enable the OMS, then manage its rules from that connection.
sourcingRulesPage.wrongConnectionTitle: This is not your OpenLinker OMS connection
